# Evaluator validation

*Generated by `report/build_report.py` from `report/validation_template.md`; numbers come from `src/validate_metrics.py` and the final labels.*

**Subset.** 40 images drawn at random (seed 123, 8 per category) from the pilot images (seeds 0-1). The list is in `data/validation_subset.json`; copies of the images are in `data/validation_subsets_images/`; the final labels are in `data/validation_labels.json` (one list per image, one 0/1/null entry per constraint in the order of `data/prompts.json`; `null` = ambiguous, excluded).

**Provenance of the labels (history, in order).**
1. First draft: written by Claude from the images (contact sheets), per constraint, before any automatic score was seen.
2. Second pass by Claude at larger image size, **not blind** (the evaluator's disagreements had already been seen): image 2 (count of three balls: three round objects, only one red) and image 9 (chair with a blue back and a red frame) became ambiguous (`null`); images 29 and 35 (yellow-green apples that look distinctly green) were relabelled as not yellow.
3. Revisions by the project owner: images 26 and 32 (the "vase is red" constraint, `null` -> 0) and image 38 (dog presence and left/right order, 0 -> `null`).
4. The corrections were merged into the single final `labels` set that all numbers below use.

[To be completed by the project owner: how many of the 40 images you checked yourself, and when.]

**Result** (`python src/validate_metrics.py --run outputs/main`; thresholds fixed in advance: presence 0.10, count 0.15):

| constraint type | n | accuracy | precision | recall | labelled positives |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| presence | 58 | 0.93 | 1.00 | 0.91 | 46 |
| binding (colour) | 37 | 0.89 | 0.93 | 0.81 | 16 |
| count | 10 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 1.00 | 5 |
| spatial | 9 | 0.89 | 1.00 | 0.50 | 2 |

Notes: presence misses are low-confidence OWL-ViT detections (partially visible horse, bench or dog); CLIP calls yellow-green apples "green" or "orange", which is why counting prompts use the count constraint alone as the primary outcome; spatial and count have very few labelled examples, so those accuracies are poorly established.
A sweep of the presence threshold (0.05-0.15) and count threshold (0.10-0.35) on the first-draft labels changed accuracy by at most 3 constraints, so the pre-set values were kept (the sweep was not repeated on the final labels).
Not evaluated: size words (small/large), because box area is not a reliable size cue.
Known biases: OWL-ViT detects stylised or partial objects less reliably; CLIP colour on a crop is affected by background and lighting; a failure to detect counts as a failure of the generation, so false negatives deflate every success rate, most for binding; the same CLIP-B/32 is used for colour and for image-text similarity.
